key_insight: At late times, flow matching toward finite training data follows nearest-sample contractions governed by distance geometry, with Voronoi interfaces controlling approximation error.
engineering_relevance: This geometry suggests tractable training targets and diagnostics that distinguish sample proximity, nearest-site retention, and feature fidelity.
method: Analyze exact trajectories against explicit exponentially contracting nearest-sample paths.
Fit the distance potential using value and gradient supervision, or fit velocities along contraction paths.
Separate transport error into initialization mismatch, velocity error, incomplete contraction, and endpoint allocation.
evidence_signal: The analysis establishes time-uniform square-root Wasserstein rates for Gaussian and fixed Gaussian-tube restarts, proves sharpness with a two-site example, and illustrates evaluation criteria on MNIST.
watch_item: Trajectory guarantees require late-time restarts away from Voronoi interfaces; mass near ties can limit distributional accuracy.
paper_title: Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning
